title: A spreadsheet-like grid for 10,000 rows
summary: Build a data grid that stays smooth with 10,000 rows and can be used fully from the keyboard.
context: Internal tools live and die by the table. The operations team at Sundial Freight, a fictional logistics company, reviews 10,000 shipment rows a day: sorting, filtering and fixing cells. Their current table freezes, scrolls with a lag, and cannot be used without a mouse.

Generate the rows yourself with a seeded script (shipment id, origin, destination, weight, status, a notes column, a date). Then build the grid. You may borrow one small free piece, such as a virtual scroller, if you name it and say what you built yourself.
Test it as a user would: open it, scroll fast, sort, edit, and put the mouse away.
must_have: Virtualised rendering: only the rows in view plus a small buffer exist in the page, and the DOM node count is visible while scrolling.

Keyboard-first navigation following the ARIA grid pattern: arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Enter to edit, Escape to cancel, Tab to move on, and a visible active cell announced to assistive technology.
Sort by any column and filter by at least two column types, without blocking the page for more than a few frames on 10,000 rows.
Editable cells with validation, and undo and redo for the last 20 edits.
Measurements in the README: scroll frame times and sort time, with the machine and browser used.
nice_to_have: Column resize and a pinned first column.
Copy and paste of a block of cells.
Row selection with shift-click and a bulk edit.
constraints: No paid services, APIs or accounts, and no commercial grid component.
Fictional data only: made-up cities, shipment ids and notes.
deliverables: A public repo created after you press Start, with commits spread across the window.
A README with how to run it and regenerate the data, your measurements, the keyboard map, and what is missing.
judge_focus: Measured performance, not claimed: where the time goes and what you changed after measuring.
Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour you actually tested, including focus after sort, filter and edit.
Which edge cases you chose to handle and which you wrote down as limits.
A trail of commits: a naive version, the measurement that showed the problem, then the fix.
bengaluru_context: Frontend platform and internal-tools teams at Bengaluru logistics, fintech and SaaS companies spend months making tables like this fast and accessible.
